findings.title: NIKKE PC launcher compromise (Nov 2026): Level Infinite CDN files modified, remote-control agent, indicators
findings.summary_md: Independent security researcher MotherSphere published a technical analysis of the NIKKE PC launcher compromise. The report alleges four JavaScript files on Level Infinite's CDN were modified on September 27, 2026 to inject a loader for insightjs.com, which from October 23 at the latest downloaded a remote-access agent called K2F on some launches. It documents indicators of compromise including the string k2f_chan in Launcher/intl_service/debug.log and a persistent Windows DLL named platform_experience_helper.dll.

findings.title: NIKKE PC launcher reportedly hit by supply-chain attack, no statement yet from Level Infinite
findings.summary_md: Inven Global reported that the NIKKE PC launcher was suspected of being used as a malware distribution vector, with no official statement yet from developer Shift Up or publisher Level Infinite. The article cites a GitHub technical report alleging attacker code was added on September 27 to JavaScript files on Level Infinite's CDN, loaded by the launcher, with potential impact for players who opened the launcher from October 24 onward.

findings.title: Goddess of Victory: NIKKE PC launcher reportedly compromised in supply-chain attack. No official confirmation from developers yet (Updated)
findings.summary_md: Automaton West reported player allegations that attackers injected malicious code into four JavaScript files on Level Infinite's CDN starting September 27, 2026, with a remote-access agent potentially installed from October 24. The article was updated on November 4 at 13:00 JST with Shift Up's statement that PC launcher script files may have been tampered with by a third party and that a client fix was implemented on November 4 at approximately 02:30 UTC+9.

findings.title: 'Is My PC Infected?' Nikke Launcher Tampering Concerns: From Attack Vector to Remediation
findings.summary_md: Inven Global covered growing concerns that running the NIKKE PC launcher may have allowed remote control of PCs, with official server files loaded by the launcher tampered with. It discusses remediation steps and notes that the attacker's fallback domain insightjs.org was registered by a third party on November 3 and replaced with a security warning in four languages.

findings.title: Hacked Nikke PC launcher spreads RAT, steals accounts and crypto data
findings.summary_md: Chosun Biz reported signs of malware distribution in the PC launcher for Goddess of Victory: NIKKE, citing a GitHub security report. The report describes four JavaScript files on Level Infinite's CDN modified as early as September 27, 2026 to inject code that could install remote-control software and steal accounts and cryptocurrency wallet data.

findings.title: NIKKE PC launcher delivered malware that let hackers control players' computers
findings.summary_md: CyberInsider reported that NIKKE updated its PC launcher after attackers injected malicious scripts capable of installing remote-access malware and stealing credentials. It notes the technical report was published on November 3 by researcher MotherSphere and draws on logs and cached files from an infected machine plus analysis of the downloaded malware.
